graphs.title: The more alkali needed to neutralise the acid, the weaker it is.
graphs.label: Concentration

experiment.aim: To find the concentration of a sodium hydroxide solution by titration with hydrochloric acid
experiment.hypothesis: The more alkali needed to neutralise the acid, the lower its concentration
controlled: Volume and concentration of the acid

steps: Put 25 cm3 of 0.1 mol/dm3 hydrochloric acid in the flask.
Hold the stopcock to run in sodium hydroxide until the indicator turns pink.
Drag the eye level with the meniscus, then press Record.
Record the volume at 10 cm3 and 40 cm3 too, and compare: only the volume at the end point gives the alkali's true concentration.
title: Titration: finding a concentration
goal: Find the concentration of sodium hydroxide from the volume needed to neutralise an acid.
note: The end point is where the indicator changes colour, and the acid and the alkali are then taken to have neutralised each other. For hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide, one mole of acid reacts with one mole of alkali.

controls.label: Alkali run in from the burette

readouts.label: Concentration worked out from this volume

worked_solution: Write the equation: HCl + NaOH gives NaCl + H2O.
The acid and the alkali react in a 1 to 1 ratio, so at the end point the moles of alkali equal the moles of acid.
Moles of acid = concentration of acid x volume of acid.
Concentration of alkali = moles of alkali / volume of alkali.
hints: The end point is where the indicator changes colour.
Read the burette with your eye level with the bottom of the meniscus.
At the end point the acid and the alkali have just neutralised each other.
